views.name: orders_with_line_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT od.orderid,
       od.productid,
       od.unitprice,
       od.quantity,
       od.discount,
       (od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS line_total,
       o.customerid,
       o.employeeid,
       o.orderdate,
       o.requireddate,
       o.shippeddate,
       o.shipvia,
       o.freight,
       o.shipcountry,
       p.productname,
       p.supplierid,
       p.categoryid,
       c.companyname AS companyname,
       e.lastname AS lastname,
       e.firstname AS firstname
FROM order_details od
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.orderid = od.orderid
LEFT JOIN products p ON p.productid = od.productid
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customerid = o.customerid
LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.employeeid = o.employeeid

params.description: Provides one row per order line (orderid, productid) with the line-level monetary amount and related order, product, customer, and employee attributes.
params.when_to_use: Analyze sales at the order-line grain (e.g., line totals, unit price, quantity, discount) across orders, products, customers, employees, or time. | Compose higher-level aggregates such as order-level totals, product-level sales, customer lifetime value by aggregating line_total. | Filter or slice order-lines by product attributes, customer attributes, employee attributes, shipping attributes, or order dates before aggregation. | Join to dimensions with a one-row-per-key cardinality (product, customer, employee) to enrich lines without duplicating measures.
params.output_schema: orderid: order identifier - from order_details.orderid | productid: product identifier - from order_details.productid | unitprice: unit price at the time of the order line - from order_details.unitprice | quantity: quantity ordered on the line - from order_details.quantity | discount: discount applied to the line (nullable) - from order_details.discount | line_total: monetary amount for the line after discount = (order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0))) - derived expression | customerid: customer who placed the order - from orders.customerid (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | employeeid: employee handling the order - from orders.employeeid (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | orderdate: order date/time - from orders.orderdate (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | requireddate: required delivery date - from orders.requireddate (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | shippeddate: shipped date/time - from orders.shippeddate (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | shipvia: shipping method/carrier id - from orders.shipvia (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | freight: freight charge for the order - from orders.freight (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | shipcountry: destination country for the order - from orders.shipcountry (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | productname: product name - from products.productname (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | supplierid: product supplier identifier - from products.supplierid (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | categoryid: product category identifier - from products.categoryid (nullable because LEFT JOIN) | companyname: customer company name - from customers.companyname (nullable because LEFT JOIN through orders) | lastname: employee last name - from employees.lastname (nullable because LEFT JOIN through orders) | firstname: employee first name - from employees.firstname (nullable because LEFT JOIN through orders)
params.grounded_columns: order_details.orderid | order_details.productid | order_details.unitprice | order_details.quantity | order_details.discount | orders.orderid | orders.customerid | orders.employeeid | orders.orderdate | orders.requireddate | orders.shippeddate | orders.shipvia | orders.freight | orders.shipcountry | products.productid | products.productname | products.supplierid | products.categoryid | customers.customerid | customers.companyname | employees.employeeid | employees.lastname | employees.firstname
params.metric: line_total = order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0))  -- per-row derived monetary measure
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to product dimension (products or product_inventory_snapshot) on productid — safe because this view is already one-row-per (orderid, productid); joining to a one-row-per-product dimension will not duplicate line_total. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customer dimension (customers or any one-row-per-customer view) on customerid — safe because customers are one row per customer; joining will not multiply line_total. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to employee dimension (employees or any one-row-per-employee view) on employeeid — safe because employees are one row per employee; joining will not multiply line_total. | cardinality-UNSAFE (avoid without re-aggregation): do NOT join directly to a table or view that is one-to-many from productid (e.g., product price history, multiple inventory snapshot rows per product) or one-to-many from orderid (e.g., another order-level line items table) without first aggregating that other dataset to the matching grain — such joins will multiply this view's rows and duplicate line_total. | cardinality-UNSAFE (avoid without re-aggregation): do NOT join to sibling aggregate views that have a different grain (e.g., orders_agg_by_order which is aggregated to order-level) by simply joining on orderid unless you plan to either (a) aggregate this view up to order-level (SUM(line_total) GROUP BY orderid) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate correctly, because mixing grains can double-count or inflate measures. | composition recommendations for building correct aggregates: to get order-level totals, aggregate line_total: SELECT orderid, SUM(line_total) AS order_total FROM orders_with_line_totals GROUP BY orderid. To get product-level sales across orders: SELECT productid, SUM(line_total) AS product_sales FROM orders_with_line_totals GROUP BY productid. When joining to other one-to-many datasets, always align grains by pre-aggregating the many-side to the one-side key before joining.

views.description: One row per order line enriched with order and product/customer/employee attributes and a derived line_total (unitprice * quantity * (1-discount)). Useful as a reusable denormalized order-line view for revenue, product performance, customer purchase, and employee sales analyses. | Use for: Total revenue by order / product / customer / employee; Order-line level profitability or revenue trends; Join-ready denormalized order lines for filtering by date, product, customer, or employee

views.name: orders_agg_by_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT od.orderid,
       COUNT(*) AS total_lines,
       SUM(od.quantity) AS total_quantity,
       SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS total_amount,
       AVG(od.unitprice) AS avg_unitprice
FROM order_details od
GROUP BY od.orderid

params.description: Pre-aggregated order-level measures computed from order_details: one row per order showing line count, quantities, amount and average unit price.
params.when_to_use: Get order-level summaries (number of lines, total quantity, total amount, average unit price) for reporting or downstream joins. | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., customer or date-level totals) by further aggregating these order-level measures. | Join to dimension tables (customers, orders header, employees) to enrich order summaries without changing the order-level measures.
params.output_schema: orderid: surrogate/key identifying the order — sourced from order_details.orderid (GROUP BY key). | total_lines: count of order detail rows for the order — COUNT(*) over order_details rows per order (derived from the rows aggregated in the view). | total_quantity: sum of quantity for the order — SUM(order_details.quantity) as aggregated in the view (grounded to order_details.quantity). | total_amount: revenue-like amount for the order — SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0))) as computed in the view (grounded to unitprice, quantity, discount columns of order_details). | avg_unitprice: average unit price across the order's detail lines — AVG(order_details.unitprice) as computed in the view (grounded to order_details.unitprice).
params.metric: total_lines = COUNT(*)  -- count of order_details rows per order (COUNT over the grouped rows in this view). | total_quantity = SUM(order_details.quantity)  -- additive measure of units per order. | total_amount = SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0)))  -- monetary measure aggregated at order level; computed per detail row then summed. | avg_unitprice = AVG(order_details.unitprice)  -- average of unitprice across detail rows for the order (not weighted by quantity).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders (orders header) on orderid — safe because this view is one-row-per-order (grain = orderid); joining will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to customers dimension/view on customerid (via orders header) — safe when joining the orders_agg_by_order rows to a single customer row per order (do this by first joining orders_agg_by_order -> orders_header on orderid to expose customerid, then join to customers on customerid). Measures remain correct because the join is 1:1 from order to customer. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to employee dimension/view on employeeid (via orders header) — safe when the orders header maps each order to a single employee; preserves measures. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views (e.g., order_details again, order-level events, shipments with multiple rows per order, product-level lines) without re-aggregation — such joins will multiply rows and therefore duplicate this view's aggregated measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relation, either (a) join on orderid and then re-aggregate the measures using SUM/AVG with appropriate weighting, or (b) aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-order before joining. | If composing to higher-level aggregates (e.g., customer totals): first ensure you have one row per order (this view satisfies that) and then SUM(total_amount) or SUM(total_quantity) grouped by customerid. Do not SUM across this view after joining to any child table that has multiple rows per order unless you deduplicate or re-aggregate. | Joining to sibling JOIN/NORM/RANK/WIN views: these are allowed if they are one-row-per-order (JOIN like orders_with_line_totals) or one-row-per-dimension; confirm their grain. Do NOT join to sibling views that are known windowed or rank outputs that produce multiple rows per order without handling multiplicity. | Planner note: the view's measures are additive at the order grain (total_lines, total_quantity, total_amount). avg_unitprice is an order-level average of unitprice (not quantity-weighted) and should not be summed across orders — to compute an overall average unit price across orders, use a weighted formula (SUM(total_amount) / SUM(total_quantity)) or recompute from base detail rows as appropriate.

views.description: One row per order aggregating its order lines to produce order-level measures: total_lines, total_quantity, total_amount (sum of line totals) and average_unitprice. Useful for analyses at the order (transaction) grain: order value distribution, average basket size, and joining back to customers/employees/shippers. | Use for: Which orders are highest value or largest by quantity; Order-level KPIs such as average basket size or order amount; Segmenting orders by total_amount or total_quantity

views.name: product_inventory_snapshot
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.productid,
       p.productname,
       p.supplierid,
       p.categoryid,
       COALESCE(p.quantityperunit, '') AS quantityperunit,
       COALESCE(p.unitprice, 0.0) AS unitprice,
       COALESCE(p.unitsinstock, 0) AS unitsinstock,
       COALESCE(p.unitsonorder, 0) AS unitsonorder,
       COALESCE(p.reorderlevel, 0) AS reorderlevel,
       p.discontinued
FROM products p

params.description: A per-product snapshot of product master (catalog) and inventory attributes from the products table.
params.when_to_use: Lookup product attributes (name, supplier, category) for a given productid or list of productids | Show current inventory and reorder-related values per product (units in stock, units on order, reorder level) | Compose product-level reporting where each product must appear once (e.g., join product attributes to sales aggregates) | Seed further aggregations or joins that need exactly one row per product
params.output_schema: productid: primary key of the view; product identifier from products.productid | productname: product display name from products.productname | supplierid: foreign key to suppliers from products.supplierid | categoryid: foreign key to categories from products.categoryid | quantityperunit: textual packaging/quantity info; COALESCE(products.quantityperunit, '') | unitprice: numeric unit price; COALESCE(products.unitprice, 0.0) | unitsinstock: integer units currently in stock; COALESCE(products.unitsinstock, 0) | unitsonorder: integer units currently on order; COALESCE(products.unitsonorder, 0) | reorderlevel: integer reorder threshold; COALESCE(products.reorderlevel, 0) | discontinued: boolean/flag from products.discontinued indicating if product is discontinued
params.grounded_columns: products.productid | products.productname | products.supplierid | products.categoryid | products.quantityperunit | products.unitprice | products.unitsinstock | products.unitsonorder | products.reorderlevel | products.discontinued
params.metric: productid = products.productid | productname = products.productname | supplierid = products.supplierid | categoryid = products.categoryid | quantityperunit = COALESCE(products.quantityperunit, '') | unitprice = COALESCE(products.unitprice, 0.0) | unitsinstock = COALESCE(products.unitsinstock, 0) | unitsonorder = COALESCE(products.unitsonorder, 0) | reorderlevel = COALESCE(products.reorderlevel, 0) | discontinued = products.discontinued
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to suppliers on supplierid — safe because product_inventory_snapshot has one row per productid; joining to the suppliers dimension (one supplier per supplierid) will not duplicate product rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to categories on categoryid — safe because categories is a one-row-per-category dimension and will not duplicate product rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to orders_agg_by_order or orders_with_line_totals only when joining on productid if those views are pre-aggregated to product-level; do NOT join directly to orders_with_line_totals (which is JOIN and likely one-to-many: order lines per product) without aggregation, because that will multiply product_inventory_snapshot rows and duplicate its inventory measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: to combine with sales metrics from sibling views, prefer joining to an orders_agg_by_order (if it is aggregated at productid) or to a derived aggregation by productid (e.g., SUM(quantity) GROUP BY productid) so that results remain one-row-per-product or are explicitly aggregated after the join. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join product_inventory_snapshot directly to any one-to-many transactional table (orders, order_lines, or orders_with_line_totals if it contains multiple lines per product/order) on productid unless you also GROUP BY productid after the join or aggregate the transactional side first — otherwise unitsinstock/unitsonorder/unitprice will be duplicated across matching transaction rows. | safe composition pattern: LEFT JOIN product_inventory_snapshot p ON p.productid = x.productid where x is a pre-aggregated table keyed by productid (one row per product) — preserves snapshot measures without duplication. | aggregation guidance: when you need product-level measures after joining to many-sided tables, compute transactional aggregates first (e.g., sales_qty_by_product = SELECT productid, SUM(quantity) FROM order_lines GROUP BY productid) then JOIN that aggregated result to product_inventory_snapshot on productid.

views.description: One row per product exposing inventory and pricing attributes cleaned/coalesced. Useful for product catalogue, stock-level alerts, and joining to sales to compute stock coverage. Provides explicit numeric defaults where NULLs might appear. | Use for: Inventory level reports and stock reordering alerts; Price lists and product catalog exports; Joining product attributes to sales to compute stock-to-sales ratios

views.name: customer_order_counts_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.customerid,
       c.companyname,
       COALESCE(oagg.total_orders, 0) AS total_orders,
       COALESCE(oagg.total_amount, 0.0) AS total_amount,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(oagg.total_amount,0.0) DESC) AS amount_rank
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT o.customerid AS customerid,
         COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS total_orders,
         SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS total_amount
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN order_details od ON od.orderid = o.orderid
  GROUP BY o.customerid
) oagg ON oagg.customerid = c.customerid

params.description: For each customer, returns the customer's id and name, the customer's total number of orders, the customer's total order dollars (sum of line-level extended price after discount), and the customer's rank by total amount (highest amount = rank 1).
params.when_to_use: Ranking customers by total purchase amount across all orders. | Reporting customer lifetime order counts and revenue (one row per customer). | Filtering or slicing customers by total_orders or total_amount before joining to other one-row-per-customer datasets. | Composing dashboards or downstream queries that need customer-level aggregates (counts, sums) and a precomputed rank to avoid recalculating window functions.
params.output_schema: customerid: the customer identifier (derived from customers.customerid). | companyname: the customer/company name (derived from customers.companyname). | total_orders: the customer's count of distinct orders (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT orders.orderid) inside the subquery oagg; COALESCE to 0 for customers with no orders). | total_amount: the customer's total amount across order lines (derived from SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount,0.0))) aggregated by orders.customerid; COALESCE to 0.0 for customers with no orders). | amount_rank: the RANK() of customer by total_amount in descending order (computed as RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(oagg.total_amount,0.0) DESC)).
params.grounded_columns: customers.customerid | customers.companyname | orders.customerid | orders.orderid | order_details.orderid | order_details.unitprice | order_details.quantity | order_details.discount
params.metric: total_orders = COUNT(DISTINCT orders.orderid) grouped by orders.customerid (in subquery oagg); nulls/absent customers coerced to 0 via COALESCE. | total_amount = SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount,0.0))) grouped by orders.customerid (in subquery oagg); nulls/absent customers coerced to 0.0 via COALESCE. | amount_rank = RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(oagg.total_amount,0.0) DESC) computed after left-joining the per-customer aggregates to customers (ties receive same rank and gaps are possible).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-customer dimension (for example, the base customers table or another view that is guaranteed to be one row per customers.customerid) on customers.customerid — safe because this view is one row per customers.customerid and joining to another one-row-per-customer preserves row-per-customer cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | Do NOT directly join this view to any one-to-many child table or view (for example orders, order_details, or other line-level datasets) without first re-aggregating the child side to customerid. Joining one-to-many will multiply total_orders and total_amount, because those measures are pre-aggregated at customer grain in this view. | If you need to join to orders or order_details for additional filters/columns, either: (a) aggregate the orders/order_details to customerid (producing one row per customer) and then join — preserves measures; or (b) join and then re-aggregate after the join, computing SUM/COUNT over the joined set and discarding the precomputed totals to avoid double-counting. | Do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that are at a lower grain (e.g., orders_agg_by_order) on orderid without re-aggregating them to customerid first — such joins will be many-to-one and will duplicate this view's customer-level measures unless the planner explicitly recognizes and handles the aggregation. | Safe composition examples: join customer_order_counts_rank to customers (on customerid) to get additional customer attributes; join to employee_sales_running_total (if that view is one-row-per-employee) via a bridging one-row-per-customer mapping to employee if present. Unsafe example: join directly to order_details (on customerid via orders) without aggregation — this will inflate totals.

views.description: One row per customer with their total_orders and total_amount (derived from order_details) and a rank by total_amount descending. Useful for top-customer reporting and downstream filtering by rank to implement Top-K customers. | Use for: Find top customers by revenue; Customer lifetime value and segmentation by total spend; Lists of customers with order counts and spend for CRM actions

views.name: employee_sales_running_total
views.body_sql:
SELECT o.orderid,
       o.employeeid,
       o.orderdate,
       SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0))) AS order_amount,
       SUM(SUM(od.unitprice * od.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(od.discount,0.0)))) OVER (PARTITION BY o.employeeid ORDER BY o.orderdate ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total_by_employee
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_details od ON od.orderid = o.orderid
GROUP BY o.orderid, o.employeeid, o.orderdate

params.description: Provides per-order sales amounts and a running cumulative sales total per employee ordered by order date.
params.when_to_use: Get the sales amount for each order and the cumulative sales for the employee up to that order. | Build reports showing how an individual employee's cumulative sales progress over time (by order). | Compose higher-level aggregates by employee or by date ranges while preserving per-order running-total context (ensure correct re-aggregation). | Join to order-level attributes (customer, ship info) when you need the order amount and running total alongside those attributes.
params.output_schema: orderid: unique identifier of the order; derived from orders.orderid (base table 'orders'). | employeeid: identifier of the employee who handled the order; derived from orders.employeeid (base table 'orders'). | orderdate: date/time when the order was placed; derived from orders.orderdate (base table 'orders'). | order_amount: total dollar amount for the order = SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0))) aggregated at the order level; computed from order_details.unitprice, order_details.quantity, order_details.discount joined to orders by orderid. | running_total_by_employee: cumulative SUM of order_amount over all orders for the same employee ordered by orderdate (includes the current order) implemented as a window SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY employeeid ORDER BY orderdate ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
params.grounded_columns: orders.orderid | orders.employeeid | orders.orderdate | order_details.unitprice | order_details.quantity | order_details.discount
params.metric: order_amount = SUM(order_details.unitprice * order_details.quantity * (1.0 - COALESCE(order_details.discount, 0.0))) GROUP BY orders.orderid | running_total_by_employee = SUM(order_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY orders.employeeid ORDER BY orders.orderdate ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) -- implemented in SQL by applying the window to the aggregated order_amount expression
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-order view/table (for example, orders_agg_by_order) on orderid — safe because this view is one-row-per-order (grain = orderid), so measures (order_amount, running_total_by_employee) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-employee dimension on employeeid (e.g., an employees dimension) — safe because joining one-row-per-employee will not multiply rows; running_total_by_employee remains correct at the order grain. | do NOT join directly to a one-to-many detail table/view (for example, order_details or any other multi-row-per-order source) without re-aggregating back to orderid first — such joins would multiply rows per order and thus inflate order_amount and corrupt running_total_by_employee. | do NOT join to sibling views that are one-to-many relative to orderid (for example, any view that returns multiple rows per order) unless you aggregate that sibling to one row per orderid before joining. | If you need employee-level or date-range aggregates (e.g., total sales per employee or cumulative sales at employee/date granularity), aggregate this view after joining (GROUP BY employeeid [, date bucket]) rather than attempting to sum running_total_by_employee directly — running_total_by_employee is a per-order cumulative measure and cannot be summed across orders without re-aggregation logic. | When joining to orders_with_line_totals (JOIN) or orders_agg_by_order (AGG): prefer joining on orderid and ensure the other view is at most one row per orderid (or is pre-aggregated) — then measures remain correct and not duplicated. | When composing into ranking or windowed analyses across employees (for example, comparing running totals across employees), use this view as the per-order input and apply additional window/aggregation steps; do not join a many-rows-per-order source first.

views.description: One row per order (or order line if joined) per employee with cumulative sales_to_date (running total) ordered by orderdate. Useful to analyze employee sales performance over time and compute period-to-date comparisons or time series of cumulative sales. | Use for: Time series of cumulative sales per employee; Period-to-date comparisons and trend visualizations for reps; Detecting whether an employee reached a sales milestone by date

views.name: order_line_amounts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  od.orderid,
  od.productid,
  od.unitprice,
  od.quantity,
  (od.unitprice * od.quantity) AS line_amount
FROM order_details AS od
grain: one row per order_details.orderid + order_details.productid (order line)
views.description: Normalized order detail lines with explicit extended amount computed as unitprice * quantity (ignoring discount). Keeps orderid/product and raw pricing/quantity so callers can aggregate at order or customer level.

views.name: customer_199x_spend_rollup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customerid AS customerid,
  SUM(ol.line_total) AS total_spent,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS orders_count,
  COUNT(ol.orderid) AS distinct_order_ids
FROM orders_with_line_totals AS ol
JOIN orders_with_line_totals AS o ON o.orderid = ol.orderid
WHERE o.orderdate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.customerid
HAVING SUM(ol.line_total) > 0

semantic_filters.orders_filter: use orders_199x_cohort to restrict orders to the desired year (ensure orders_with_line_totals is pre-filtered to that cohort)

views.description: Customer-level spending rollup for a specified year window: sums line amounts (unitprice * quantity) across all order lines for each customer's orders in the window. Exposes customer id and total_spent so callers can join to thresholds or compute distributions.

views.name: orders_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.employeeid,
  o.orderdate,
  o.requireddate,
  o.shippeddate,
  o.shipcountry,
  o.freight
FROM orders o
WHERE o.employeeid IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.employeeid: IS NOT NULL  -- exclude orders without an assigned employee for analyses by employee

views.description: Canonical, cleaned row-level orders relation exposing key order columns and normalized date/employee fields for downstream aggregation and late-shipment logic.

views.name: order_lateness_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.orderid,
  o.employeeid,
  CASE WHEN o.shippeddate IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_shipped,
  CASE WHEN o.shippeddate IS NOT NULL AND o.shippeddate >= o.requireddate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late,
  o.requireddate,
  o.shippeddate
FROM orders o
WHERE o.employeeid IS NOT NULL
grain: orderid  -- one row per order with lateness flags

semantic_filters.employeeid: IS NOT NULL  -- keep only orders attributable to employees

views.description: Per-order boolean flags and normalized timestamps indicating whether an order counts as 'late' (shipped and shippeddate >= requireddate) and exposes raw shipped/required dates for flexible late definitions.

views.name: employee_order_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.employeeid AS employeeid,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderid) AS total_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN olf.is_shipped = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shipped_orders_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN olf.is_late = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN olf.is_late = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_order_percentage_numerator,
  SUM(CASE WHEN olf.is_shipped IN (0,1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_order_percentage_denominator
FROM orders_base o
JOIN order_lateness_flags olf ON o.orderid = olf.orderid
WHERE o.employeeid IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.employeeid

semantic_filters.employeeid: IS NOT NULL  -- exclude NULL/unknown employee groups

views.description: Aggregated order-level measures per employee: total orders, shipped orders, late orders, and raw late percentage numerator/denominator to support ranking and thresholds.
